newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes still hamstrung by arb.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes still hamstrung by arb.

text.p: The narrow trans-Atlantic arbitrage continued to hamstring foreign crude business into the U.S. Friday, with less expensive domestic grades remaining in the spotlight.
The spread between January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent hovered around 75-80 cents, up five cents from late Thursday.
The corresponding February month also climbed five cents from Thursday to 95 cents to $1.00.

The U.S. Gulf Coast remains an elusive target for trans-Atlantic cargoes, although Brent continues to reach the U.S. East Coast and some has been moved out of storage in the Caribbean to Gulf Coast refiners, traders said.
Light Louisiana Sweet grade has cashed in on the closed arb window, trading around 84-86 cents premium to West Texas Intermediate over the day. The grade hit WTI plus $1.10 earlier in the week.
In the U.S. aftermarket, three partial outright January Brent trades fell between $22.92-98 a barrel, down 10 cents from the IPE settlement.
